title: Detect the macos.binary.arm64 package type used by R-devel 4.7 on macOS
description:
R-devel (4.7.0) on macOS arm64 reports `.Platform$pkgType` as `macos.binary.arm64`, whose `<system>` is `macos`, not the `macosx` that `pkg_type_system_for_os()` returns for darwin.

`current_r_custom_pkg_type()` compared the two with `identical()`, so it dropped the type from the platform name and pkgcache looked for binaries in `bin/macosx/sonoma-arm64/contrib/4.7`. CRAN has moved those to `bin/macos/arm64/contrib/4.7` and the old directory no longer has a 4.7 subdirectory, so metadata and downloads 404.

Fixed by treating `macos` as a valid package-type system on darwin, alongside `macosx`. pkgcache then keeps the type in the platform name and derives `bin/macos/arm64/contrib/<x.y>` from it.

(For the records, related to <https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/909>.)

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to pkgcache website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the pkgcache website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Add support for sourcing repository credentials from the keyring
description:
This commit updates both the metadata and package caches to support downloading packages and package indexes from repositories that require HTTP basic authentication to access.

Initial support for these authenticated repositories is very narrow: the repository URL must contain a username, no password, and have an entry in the system keyring. We also don't make any attempt to prompt users for credentials when requests fail.

Unit tests are included for the new authentication header helpers, but there are currently no tests of end-to-end workflows with an authenticated repository, and I may have missed something.

Part of r-lib/pak#729.

title: Rewrite Bioconductor repo handling
description:
Put all bioc-related code in a separate, standalone file, which only has a single object, called `bioconductor`. This is a list of functions, and serves as an API.

This file is completely standalone and can be embedded into other packages. Most notably, remotes and renv could make use of it.

Still needs some docs and tests, I need to figure out how to do these, in a nice standalone way.

About the implementation:
1. It has a builtin map, to map R versions to BioC versions. This map includes the R versions whose mapping will not change any more. It does not include 3.6, because that will change to a new BioC version, when that comes out later this year.
2. A "parser" that can read the https://bioconductor.org/config.yaml file. We use this if the builtin map does not have the information we need. The parser is similar to what Bioconductor uses in the BiocManager package, so we expect it to keep working in the future, even though it is not a proper yaml parser.
3. The contents of the `config.yaml` file and also other pieces are cached in the file's own environment.
4. We also fix some mistakes with the previous bioc code, e.g. add the BioCworkflows repository.
5. The R_BIOC_VERSION env var can override the mapped bioc version.
6. The bioc mirror can be also specified via an env var and an option. (Option takes priority.)
7. One can also obtain the `config.yaml` file externally (e.g. if one needs async IO to get it), and then use `set_yaml_config()` to push it into the `bioconductor` object.

Closes #23
